##Assignment

R has three assignment operators:

- `->`  
- `=`  
- `<-`

```{r aassignments}
x1 = 5
5 -> x2
x3 = 7

cat("The value of x1 is:", x1)
```

##Atomic Vectors

Atomic Vectors are 1D data structures, where all vaues in them hav eyo have th same data type. For example, if we do the following:

```{r atomic}
mixed_vec = c('ISA' , 401)

mixed_num = c(401L, 3.14)

print(typeof(mixed_num))
print(typeof(mixed_vec))
```

From this output, if you have multiple data types. R will use the most general representation for them.

##Lists
```{r list}
lst <- list( # list constructor/creator
  1:3, # atomic double/numeric vector  of length = 3
  "a", # atomic character vector of length = 1 (aka scalar)
  c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), # atomic logical vector of length = 3
  c(2.3, 5.9) # atomic double/numeric vector of length =3
)
lst # printing the list

from_list_to_sublist2 = 1st




## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
